title: The Lyra Technique II: SVD Denoising and Persona Intensity in KV-Cache Geometry, with Its Emotion Channel Corrected
subtitle: Version 1.1 (2026-11-01): the W_K emotion channel is corrected at source and withdrawn as a reading of model or user state; SVD denoising gains are upper bounds
abstract: Version 1.1, corrected 2026-11-01. The emotion channel this paper reported as W_K directional projection is corrected at source: the probe applied no W_K (it was a class-mean key readout), and its labels are the emotion a generator was asked to write into a third-person story, not the user's or the model's state. On 30 classes it scores 0.410 against a text (TF-IDF) baseline's 0.370 (Holm p = 0.071, not significant; 0.348 with FWL fitted on the training fold), and the method as described scores 0.358 against 0.382. The binary AUROC 0.992 beats text (0.963, Holm p = 0.006), but on ten emotions (n = 300), confounded with arousal; the injection test is withdrawn. SVD denoising appears to reveal hidden signal, raising persona intensity from AUROC 0.611-0.751 to 0.899-0.992; however, the denoising deltas fall within the max-over-rank selection envelope (0/16 exceed it), so the raw AUROCs are the defensible numbers and the denoised values are reported as upper bounds pending nested CV. Dominant singular values carry scale; residual values carry discriminative structure. Denoising is a calibration tool, not a universal amplifier.
